name: Reprieve
oracle_text:
Return target spell to its owner's hand.
Draw a card.
blocked_sentences: Return target spell to its owner's hand.

needs.what: a way to move a *targeted spell* off the stack into its owner's hand -- either a new op that reads `ctx.target_sids(target)` (the way `counter` does), removes that StackItem and moves its backing object to Zone.HAND, or `return_to_hand` taught to accept a `kind: "spell"` target. It must not be a counter: 701.5a bouncing is not countering, so it works on a spell with "this spell can't be countered", it fires no spell-countered event, and the card goes to hand rather than to the graveyard
needs.why_existing_wont_do: `counter` is the only op that consumes a spell target, and its destination is hardwired -- `op_counter` moves the object to Zone.GRAVEYARD with cause="countered", emits SPELL_COUNTERED, and refuses uncounterable spells; it takes no destination key, so it cannot be aimed at a hand and would be a different card in three observable ways. `return_to_hand` reaches the right zone but cannot be aimed at a spell: a `kind: "spell"` target produces a `TargetRef.stack(sid)`, and `resolve_pool`'s `{"target": "t1"}` branch calls `ctx.target_oids`, which keeps only `kind == "object"` refs -- so the pool is empty and the op is a silent no-op. Verified in the sandbox: with `return_to_hand` on `{"target": "t1"}` the targeted dummy creature spell resolved onto the opponent's battlefield untouched, and the card still passed all six gates, which is exactly the quiet wrong-card failure a gap record exists to avoid. Selecting the spell without targeting (`objects: {"zone": "stack"}`) does move it -- `_remove_from_zone` drops the StackItem correctly -- but it is untargeted, would sweep every spell on the stack, and drops the printed "target", so ward/hexproof/heroic and "can't be the target of spells" all stop applying.
